title: Buffered and unbuffered channels: the choice that causes deadlock

videos.script: A channel made with no size has no room at all. This lesson is about what that means. {{meet}} A sender reaches its send at zero milliseconds. The receiver turns up at three hundred. The send waits the whole time, and returns only when the value has crossed. The two goroutines meet, and that meeting is the synchronisation. {{buffer}} Give the channel room for three, and the picture changes. Three sends return at once. The fourth waits for a free slot. After that, the sender moves at the receiver's pace. A buffer absorbs a burst. It does not make a slow consumer fast. {{loud}} Then deadlock. Main sends with nobody to receive, and the runtime stops the program with a fatal error. {{quiet}} Last, the dangerous version. One goroutine is stuck, but main is still busy. No error. No message. The goroutine just stays there. {{close}} Lesson 5 gives a goroutine a way to wait on several channels at once.
